relevance_note: First report of germline TNFAIP3 loss-of-function mutations in identifiable patients, e.g. 'shared between patients P4 and P6, including a novel variant in TNFAIP3'.
method_note: Read the full Markdown by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON, pulled the Table 1 cells by splitting each family row, and checked every span against the paper (Table 1 transcription checked by eye against the table). Supplementary Table 1 (individual clinical data) and the pedigrees (Fig. 1a) are not in the file, so most individual-level detail is unavailable. Table 1 rows are families, not people, so each family's variant is attached to every person the text ties to that family. Labels: the paper labels only P4, P5, P6 and P9 in text; Family 1's affected mother and two daughters, the three unaffected Family 2 members, the screened patient of each of Families 3-5, and the Family 6 mother and two daughters have no printed labels and are 'unnamed person 1-12' in order of first mention (rule 2 could not give distinct labels to two unlabelled daughters of an unlabelled mother). 'Patient 6' (Fig. 5c, summary) is taken to be P6. P9 (Fig. 2d) is a study patient whose family is not stated; P9 may be the same person as one of the unnamed persons 7-12 (or another family member), but the paper does not say so, so P9 is kept as a separate row with variant 'not reported'. Families 3 and 5 are listed as 'Dominant' and Family 1's 'maternal unaffected family members' were sequenced, but these further relatives are not described or counted, so they get no rows. The three unaffected Family 2 members were Sanger-sequenced and the variant 'segregated with the inflammatory phenotype'; their non-carrier status is implied, not stated, so they have no variant rows. Family 1 is described at family level only ('a dominant disorder manifesting early-onset systemic inflammation, arthralgia/arthritis, oral/genital ulcers and ocular inflammation'); these features are not attributed to individual Family 1 members, so their checklists are 'not reported'. 'oral/genital ulcers' (P4, P5, P6, 'had in common') is read as both oral and genital ulcers for the checklist. P6 'elevated inflammatory markers' is marked observed because anakinra 'normalized markers of systemic inflammation in Patient 6'; the markers are not named. Group exclusions: 'an overt autoimmune disease was only diagnosed in Patient 6' and 'none of our patients have developed lymphomas or other malignancies' were applied to every variant carrier in the study (not to the unstudied sister of P6 or the unaffected relatives); the autoimmune exclusion was not carried down to specific checklist autoimmune items. 'five patients in our study developed autoantibodies' and the Fig. 4c 'absence of clinical allergic disease' are counts or unnamed groups and were not assigned. Inheritance is 'not reported' for everyone (rule 8): Table 1 lists Family 4 as 'De novo' but the paper does not describe parental testing; the daughters in Families 1, 2 and 6 share their mother's variant but the paper does not state the variant's origin. Variant type is recorded only where the authors name it for a specific variant (Family 6 'frameshift'); the per-family types are otherwise only implied by HGVS. Protein for Family 2 is taken from the text ('p.Phe224Serfs*4'); Table 1 prints 'p. Phe224Serfs*4' with a space. Genome build for the chr6 coordinates is not printed. Contradictions/inconsistencies: Family 2 is 'a family of Italian ancestry' in the text but 'European American' in Table 1; Family 1 is 'Caucasian' in the text and 'European Canadian' in Table 1 (both recorded); the text says 'In total, we identified 5 heterozygous truncating mutations in TNFAIP3 in five families' while Table 1 and the abstract list six families. A novel TNFRSF9 variant also 'remained in consideration' in Family 1, but it is a candidate without a printed description or clear per-person attribution, so it is not recorded. No age, vital status or consanguinity is stated for anyone. n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated are null: no total is stated (Online Methods gives 7 NIH, 4 Utrecht and 2 Hacettepe patients; screening cohorts were 150 patients and 384 Turkish plus 384 Japanese Behcet's cases).
